newsitem.title: USA: USDA - No confirmation of China exporting corn.
newsitem.headline: USDA - No confirmation of China exporting corn.

text.p: Top U.S. Agriculture Department officials said Wednesday they have no confirmation that the Chinese government is going to relax its current ban on corn exports, but said they are actively pursuing reports of such action.
USDA Secretary Dan Glickman said he did not want to comment on what impact a restarting of Chinese corn exports may have until he had more information.
"We're actively pursuing those reports," said USDA Foreign Agriculture Service Administrator Gus Schumacher.

Schumacher and Glickman were asked by reporters about a report by the private news agency World Perspectives that the Chinese government is considering allowing limited corn exports of up to two million tonnes.
China in the last few years has switched from being a major corn exporter to being an importer of U.S. corn.
Analysts have said that a bumper corn harvest in China this year could ease supply shortages and reduce imports.
The two USDA officials were at a press conference at which 18 state agriculture commissioners announced their support for President Clinton.
